translations.text: When Jesus drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives: and the rest.
Christ's Passion was read just now before us, but we wish first to tell you now how he came to the city of Jerusalem and drew near to his own death, and would not avoid the Passion by flight.
"The Saviour went to the city of Jerusalem, and when he drew near to the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, saying thus,
"Go to the town that is opposite you, and you will at once find an ass tied up, and its foal with it. Untie them and lead them to me," and so on.

It had become known to the people that a little before, the Saviour had raised Lazarus from death, who had lain stinking for four nights in the tomb. Then those who were believers came out to meet Christ with that honour, as we said before.

Some unbelievers came too, not with any honour but with great anger, as John the Evangelist said: "The chief men of the people considered among themselves that they would kill Lazarus, whom Christ had raised from death."
because many of the people believed in the Saviour through the dead man's resurrection." We will now begin the exposition of this reading.
The two disciples whom Christ sent for the ass signified the teachers whom God sent to teach mankind.
There were two of them because of what this signifies about what a teacher must have. He must have learning, so that he can teach God's people with wisdom in the right faith,
And he must set the people a good example with good works, and so with these two things, that is, with teaching and good example, always bend the lay people to God's will.
The tied ass and her foal signify two peoples, that is, the Jewish and the heathen:
I say heathen because all mankind was at that time still living in heathendom, except only the Jewish people, who kept the old law in that time.
They were tied because all mankind was bound with sins, just as the prophet said, "Every man is bound with the ropes of his sins."
Then God sent his apostles and their successors to bound mankind, and commanded them to untie them and lead them to him. How did they untie the ass and the foal?
They preached the right faith and God's commandments to the people, and also confirmed their preaching with great miracles.
Then the people turned from the devil's service to the worship of Christ, and were released from all sins through holy baptism, and led to Christ.
The ass is a stupid beast, and unclean, and more lacking in reason than other beasts, and strong for carrying burdens.
So, before Christ's coming, men were foolish and unclean, when they served idols and various vices, and bowed to the images that they themselves had made, and said to them, "You are my God."
And whatever burden the devil set upon them, they bore it. But when Christ came to mankind, he turned our foolishness to wisdom, and our uncleanness to pure ways of life.
The tamed ass signified the Jewish people, who were tamed under the old law. The wild foal signified all the other people, who were still heathen and untamed;
but they became tamed and believing when Christ sent his disciples throughout the whole world, saying thus, "Go throughout the whole world, and teach all nations,
and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; and command that they keep all the commandments that I have taught you."
The owner of the asses asked why they were untying his asses. In the same way, the chief men of every nation wished to oppose God's preaching perversely.

But when they saw that the messengers, through God's might, healed the lame and the blind, and gave speech to the dumb, and also raised the dead to life, they could not withstand those miracles, but all together turned to God.
Christ's disciples said, "The Lord has need of the asses, and will send them back again."
They did not say "Our Lord" or "Your Lord," but simply "the Lord"; for Christ is Lord of all lords, both of men and of all creatures.
They said, "He will send them back again." We are urged and invited to God's kingdom, but we are not compelled.
When we are called, we are untied; and when we are left to our own choice, it is as if we were sent back.
It is God's mercy that we are untied; but if we live rightly, that is both God's gift and also our own diligence.
We must always pray for the Lord's help, because our own choice makes no progress unless it is furthered by the Almighty.
Christ did not order a proud steed adorned with golden trappings to be brought to him, but he chose the humble ass to carry him;
for he always taught humility, and gave the example of it in himself, and said thus: "Learn from me, for I am gentle and very humble, and you will find rest for your souls."
This was prophesied about Christ, as were all the things that he did, before he was born as a man.
Zion is a mountain, and its name means 'place of watching'; and Jerusalem means 'vision of peace.'

The daughter of Zion is the congregation of believing people, who belong to the heavenly Jerusalem, in which there is always the vision of peace, without any strife; the Saviour will bring us there if we follow him.
Christ's disciples laid their garments on the ass, because he would not ride on a bare ass.
Garments signify works of righteousness, as the prophet said, "Lord, your priests are clothed with righteousness."
The bare ass is saddled with garments when the empty man is adorned for God's hand by the admonitions and examples of wise teachers;
and he then carries Christ, as the apostle said, "You have been bought at a great price; therefore glorify and carry God in your body."
We carry God in our body, because we are the temple and vessel of the Holy Spirit, if we guard ourselves against foul sins;
concerning which the same apostle said very fearsomely, "Whoever defiles God's temple, God will destroy him."
He who is not God's temple is the devil's temple, and carries a very heavy burden on his back.
We will tell you a parable. No man can make himself king, but the people have the choice to choose as king whomever pleases them;
But after he has been consecrated as king, then he has power over the people, and they cannot shake his yoke from their necks.
so too every man has his own choice, before he sins, whether he will follow the devil's will or refuse it.
But if he binds himself with the devil's works, he cannot unbind himself by his own power, unless Almighty God unbinds him with the strong hand of his mercy.
By his own will and his own negligence he is bound, but through God's mercy he is unbound, if he afterwards earns that release from God.
The people who threw their garments under the ass's feet are the martyrs, who for faith in Christ gave their own bodies up to torments.
Some of them were burned in fire, some drowned in the sea, and killed with various tortures;
and they gave us an example that we must not, because of any persecutions or hardships, abandon our faith and turn away from Christ, any more than they did.
Of this the apostle Paul said, "All heavenly and earthly things were to be restored in Christ."
Then the chief men grew envious of his teaching, and plotted with much deliberation how they might bring him to death.

Death could not have come near him if he himself had not willed it, but he came to men because he wished to be obedient to his Father even to death, and to redeem mankind from eternal death through his temporary death.
Then it happened to the cruel devil as it does to the greedy fish, which sees the bait and does not see the hook that is stuck in the bait.
And then about the ninth hour, when he had died, two believing men, Joseph and Nicodemus, came and buried his body before evening in a new tomb, wrapped in costly garments.
And his body lay in the tomb on Saturday night and Sunday night; and during that time the divinity was in hell, and bound the old devil, and took Adam from him,
and the servants of God must sing the hymn that the Jewish people sang to welcome Christ when he was approaching his Passion.
Now we must keep our palm until the singer begins the offertory chant, and then offer the palm to God, for the sake of what it signifies.
then they will be brought to eternal life, and then it will be as if their end were a beginning; for they will not be dead, but will be turned from death to life.
